cards.explanation: The answer is right into the high priest's courtyard, friends. Peter, one of Jesus' followers, stays back at a distance, but he doesn't stop. He walks right in and sits down with the officers (Mark 14:54). I'd have quit at the first corner and called it a nice evening stroll.

The word is warms, friends. Peter sits with the officers and warms himself by the fire (Mark 14:54). Just a man at a fire, right in the middle of the officers. I've stood next to my oven the same way, minus the officers.

The answer is False. The chief priests and the whole Sanhedrin are seeking testimony against Jesus to put Him to death, but they do not find any (Mark 14:55). They go looking and come back with nothing solid. Not a crumb.

The answer is False. Many bore false witness against Jesus, but their testimony was inconsistent (Mark 14:56). Their stories don't line up. That's many witnesses, and still they did not find any testimony.

The answer is that He would destroy the temple and build another in three days. That's the claim, friends. Some men stand up and testify falsely against Him: “We heard Him say, ‘I will destroy this man-made temple, and in three days I will build another that is made without hands.’…” Then the text adds, “But even their testimony was inconsistent.” So this is what they say, and even it doesn't hold together (Mark 14:57–59).

The answer is that He stays silent. The text says Jesus remained silent and made no reply. The high priest asks, “Have You no answer?” and still Jesus says nothing (Mark 14:60–61). I'll be honest, I couldn't hold quiet through a squeaky drawer.

The answer is True. Asked, “Are You the Christ, the Son of the Blessed One?” Jesus says, “I am.” After all that silence, it's a short, plain answer. Then He keeps going: “and you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of Power and coming with the clouds of heaven” (Mark 14:61–62).
The answer is that he tears them. The high priest tears his clothes and declares, “Why do we need any more witnesses?” (Mark 14:63). That's a big move in front of the whole council.
The word is blasphemy, friends. The high priest says, “You have heard the blasphemy. What is your verdict?” (Mark 14:64). That's the charge he puts on the table. And the council takes it from there.
The answer is False. The text says they all condemned Him as deserving of death (Mark 14:64). Not some of them, all of them. I think this is a heavy one. And friends, the story isn't over.
The answer is that she says, “You also were with Jesus the Nazarene.” She's one of the servant girls of the high priest. She looks at Peter and spots him warming himself by the fire (Mark 14:66–67).

The answer is that he says he doesn't know what she means. Peter says, “I do not know or even understand what you are talking about…” (Mark 14:68). That's the first of the three denials. It's a hard sentence to read.
The answer is that the rooster crows. Peter goes out to the gateway and the rooster crowed (Mark 14:68). That's the first crow, friends. Remember it, because it matters later.

The answer is True. This time the servant girl speaks to those standing nearby, saying, “This man is one of them” (Mark 14:69). Before, she talked straight to Peter. Now she's telling everyone else around.
The word is denies, friends. The text says he denied it again (Mark 14:70). That's twice now. I think you can hear how hard it's getting for him.
The word is Galilean, someone from Galilee. Those standing nearby say, “Surely you are one of them, for you too are a Galilean” (Mark 14:70). Now they give a reason. The word 'too' is in the text.
The answer is False. Peter began to curse and swear, “I do not know this man of whom you speak!” (Mark 14:71). That's the third time he says no. It's the hardest of the three to read.

The answer is three, friends. Peter remembers what Jesus had told him: “Before the rooster crows twice, you will deny Me three times” (Mark 14:72). Three times is exactly how many it was. Jesus said it, and it happened.

The answer is that he breaks down and weeps. Peter remembers the word Jesus had spoken to him: “Before the rooster crows twice, you will deny Me three times” (Mark 14:72). I think that's a man whose heart just broke. A sad moment, and an honest one. And friends, the story isn't over.
